$comment: The one declaration of what mutation testing covers and the floor each scope must hold. scripts/run-mutation.mjs runs a scope by name and fails below its break; tests/architecture/mutation-covers-source.arch.test.ts checks no source file falls outside both maps, that every scope declares a floor, and that package.json has a script per scope. framework's floor was 93; it measured 92.7 at this branch's head with --force, so its floor is 92. Globs, never file lists: a list goes stale the day a file is added, and the score does not drop, because the mutants that would have died were never generated. update measured 100 at this branch's head with --force, so its floor is 100. recipes mutates its domain and its application: ValidateRecipes holds the ordering and dedupe of files, the read-error mapping, the extension check, the link cache and every link finding, so it is mutated as it was when it sat in the framework scope. It measured 93.7 at this branch's head with --force, so its floor is 93. A floor is raised to the measured score after a run, never lowered without the reason here. A scope's mutate is one glob or a list where a leading ! excludes; tools is split one scope per tool profile: a profile is a static declaration whose every mutant reruns each test that loads it, and the five together outlasted every other scope on a two-core runner; vscode's single file stays with the rest. distribution held a floor of 77 before its adapters moved in and its use cases were renamed; it measured 82.1 at this branch's head with --force, so its floor is 82. The runtime and framework scores come from CI, not from this run. canary mutates a fixture, not the product: its static mutant stops a module from loading, which Stryker's vitest runner scores as survived on its own; its dynamic mutants check exact selection through nested suites, repeated spaces, and regex characters. The scope requires 100 and exactly each dynamic mutant's covering test, so a Stryker or Vitest upgrade cannot quietly bypass tests/helpers/unloadable-file-as-failed-test.ts or widen or lose mutation test selection.

excluded.src/contexts/update/application/**: Three one-call use cases over ports: each reads a decision or a cache entry from a double and returns it, so a mutant here dies only to the assertion that already pins the call. The branching they dispatch on is the domain scope's, which is mutated.
excluded.src/contexts/update/infrastructure/**: Adapters over the npm registry, the package managers and the cache file. What they translate is held by the contract suites against a local server and stub binaries; mutating them reruns those servers and subprocesses for every mutant, and the exact strings are pinned by the adapter tests.
excluded.src/contexts/update/ports/**: Interfaces and types only: they compile to nothing, so no mutant can be generated that a test could see.
excluded.src/contexts/recipes/infrastructure/**: One adapter over the disk. What it translates, the error codes and the directory listing, is held by the contract suite run against it and against the in-memory fake, and its descriptor handling by its integration test; mutating it reruns real temp directories for every mutant.
excluded.src/contexts/recipes/ports/**: Interfaces and types only: they compile to nothing, so no mutant can be generated that a test could see.
excluded.src/cli.ts: The entry point. It registers commands and returns: no branch a mutant could change that a unit or integration test would see, and what proves it runs is the e2e suite, which mutation excludes because it spawns a built binary no mutant reaches.
excluded.src/composition/**: The composition root of the migrated contexts: it constructs adapters and hands them to commands, with no rule of its own. What drives it is the in-process command tests and the e2e suite, which the mutation run leaves out (vitest.mutation.config.ts), so every mutant here would survive for a reason that says nothing about the tests.
